ops.title: deletions.py rm guard INTEGRATED onto evt.cmd (landed main b65dfe88)
ops.body: 2026-07-19: per user directive, rewrote builtin_packs/general/hooks/deletions.py from rewrite_command_occurrences(visit=) onto evt.cmd.calls('rm') — Target predicates for blast-radius (is_fs_root/is_home/contains_repo/is_repo_root/in_repo/is_scratch), targets.expand() for the glob cap, call.sub('rm', shlex.quote(trash), args=call.targets) for the trash rewrite. All 16 inline threat-model tests preserved verbatim + green (222 total, 0 fail). Note the packs relocated to captain_hook/builtin_packs/ in the 11.0.0 reorg (packs/ now holds only loader modules). MITIGATION BOUNDARY vs the 7 cmd.py holes (note a7f5f2b): the guard fails CLOSED on unverified (value=None) and incomplete/substituted targets — so rm $HOME, brace, xargs-empty are blocked at the consumer. BUT holes where the rm call is never SURFACED (bash -c "rm -rf $HOME" tainted-payload → calls('rm')==[]; process substitution <(rm -rf /)) are NOT mitigated here — my guard never sees an empty result. Those STILL require the cmd.py _calls fail-closed fix (the separate agent's work). Once cmd.py surfaces those calls, deletions.py catches them automatically.
